title: Upstream crosslink request: prompt-injection seam in kickoff/swarm dispatch prompt assembly (consumer-tool context injection)

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: CONTRACT-NAMED UPSTREAM CAPABILITY REQUIREMENT (the injection seam). vsdd's conformance architecture is injection-by-construction: the phase primer, composed domain personas, and supplements must be INJECTED into the dispatched agent's prompt (availability-is-not-activation; the cargo-cult founding incident). When kickoff/swarm dispatches, CROSSLINK assembles the agent prompt (KICKOFF.md protocol + rules injection) and exposes no hook for a consuming tool to add content — the contract records that the dispatch primitive 'carries none of the vsdd layer' and names kickoff prompt-assembly as the candidate seam. ASK: an injection point (flag/file/extension, e.g. --inject-context <file>) on kickoff run/plan and swarm, woven into the generated prompt. This gates vsdd riding kickoff/swarm at all — the #845 remediation's critical path. Until it exists the only conformant dispatch path is the runtime-harness Agent/Workflow fallback (the calcified deviation #845 remediates).

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED UPSTREAM (verified from the commit diff, dollspace-gay/crosslink 26ee1885, merged 2026-08-01, PR #44 / gh#43 'configurable kickoff prompt template via hook-config.json'): kickoff run now checks hook-config.json 'agent.kickoff_template' (a file path, resolved relative to .crosslink/) and uses that file's content as the ENTIRE agent prompt, bypassing build_prompt; 'agent.no_template: true' yields an empty prompt (run.rs step 5; utils.rs read_kickoff_template/read_no_template). This IS a workable seam for the vsdd layer: the orchestrator controls the template file and can regenerate it per dispatch with the composition+primer+personas baked in. THREE CAVEATS narrow the remaining ask: (1) REPLACE, not INJECT — the custom path loses crosslink's own built prompt entirely (15-step protocol, issue id, branch, design-doc content, conventions, verify-level steps; no placeholder interpolation), so vsdd must re-author the crosslink half too and it drifts as upstream evolves; ask remains: an append/injection mode or placeholder interpolation so crosslink's half stays tool-maintained. (2) Config-level, not dispatch-level — one template path in hook-config.json races under parallel dispatches with different compositions; ask: a per-dispatch --template flag on kickoff run/plan. (3) Nothing for swarm — the template hook is kickoff-run only. Same commit also adds 'agent.binary' (swap claude for another CLI; non-claude gets prompt via stdin, Anthropic env/credential mounts gated). NOT addressed by this commit: #852 (no effort/thinking-budget flag), #837/#846/#847/#848/#849/#850 untouched. Our local mirror (6b4f736f, 2026-07-31) predates this — re-audit after next pull.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Design input for the injection seam posted to the fork epic: https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/crosslink/issues/2#issuecomment-5154089077 — five consumer requirements (R1 interpolation/append keeping crosslink's half tool-maintained; R2 per-dispatch --template flag; R3 swarm per-agent composition incl. the uniform-clobber hazard + the exec-hook end-state; R4 coherence with the #61 dial design; R5 the assembled prompt stays auditable via KICKOFF.md). Suggested split: R1+R2 as a small fork-authored PR (the #44 pattern); R3+R4 into the #61 design cycle. The PR itself is pure crosslink work — it lives in the crosslink estate, not here.
